dst: CLASS OBJECTIVE
What will we do today?
Informatics and Computer Science · 6th grade · class 011
By the end of the class, the student will be able to:
•  explain what a computer network is and what resources are;
•  distinguish between PAN, LAN, MAN, and WAN networks;
•  differentiate between client-server and P2P networks;
•  explain the role of providers and network equipment;
•  break down a web address and explain the role of DNS.
Key concepts
network · resources · provider · client-server · P2P · IP address · domain
Check

What comes to your mind first when someone says 'network'?

src: Personal Area Network — лична мрежа, неколико метара (нпр. Bluetooth слушалице).
Local Area Network — локална мрежа: соба, зграда или школа.
Metropolitan Area Network — градска мрежа: један град.
Wide Area Network — широка мрежа: држава или свет; интернет је највећа.
Пример: пет рачунара у кабинету повезано каблом на switch → жична LAN.
Која мрежа је најмања, а која највећа? Где припада интернет?
dst: PAN · LAN · MAN · WAN
Types of networks by size
Informatics and Computer Science · 6th grade · class 011
PAN
Personal Area Network — personal network, a few meters (e.g., Bluetooth headphones).
LAN
Local Area Network — local network: room, building, or school.
MAN
Metropolitan Area Network — city network: one city.
WAN
Wide Area Network — wide network: country or world; the internet is the largest.
Example: five computers in a classroom connected by cable to a switch → wired LAN.
DISCUSSION
Which network is the smallest, and which is the largest? Where does the internet belong?

dst: ROLES IN THE NETWORK
Client-server or P2P?
Informatics and Computer Science · 6th grade · class 011
Client-server

•  there is a 'main' computer — server
•  the server stores resources and manages the network
•  clients request services
•  example: school classroom, website
P2P (peer to peer)

•  all computers are equal
•  each can share and use resources
•  there is no central server
•  example: file sharing between two phones
DISCUSSION
Which model do you recognize in the school classroom? Who is the server, and who is the client?

dst: PROVIDERS
How does the internet come to us?
Informatics and Computer Science · 6th grade · class 011
•  a provider is an organization that provides access to the internet;
•  provides connection, IP address, and a certain speed;
•  a home router connects devices to the provider;
•  without a provider, there is no access to the internet.
REMEMBER

The internet is not 'in the computer'.

It is a network of networks that you reach through a provider.
DISCUSSION
How does the internet come to your home? What is needed for it to work?

dst: ADDRESSING
IP address — unique address of a device
Informatics and Computer Science · 6th grade · class 011
An IPv4 address has four octets from 0 to 255, separated by dots.
Correct address
Incorrect addresses
Check goes octet by octet:
•  four numbers separated by dots;
•  each number is in the range 0–255;
•  256 and 300 are greater than 255 → addresses are incorrect;
•  the address must be unique in the network.
DISCUSSION
Why must a device's address be unique in the network?

dst: ADDRESSING
DNS — how a name is converted to an address
Informatics and Computer Science · 6th grade · class 011
Computers on the network communicate using IP addresses, while we remember names.
1. You type the domain
www.mojaskola.edu.rs
2. DNS translates
finds the server's IP address
3. The request goes further
the computer connects to that IP address
DNS is like a directory: with a name, you find a number. Without it, we would have to remember numbers.
DISCUSSION
What would happen if DNS didn't work?
